non_blocking_notes: docs/adr/0012 line 17 is now 102 characters while its neighbours wrap at 76-89. The substitution is correct and markdown is not covered by the format gate, but a re-wrap of that paragraph would keep the ADR visually consistent. Purely cosmetic; not worth another commit on its own.

In usgs_nwis/generate_catalogue.py:761 the locals unpacked from _matching_coverage remain named start_date/end_date while being emitted under the new canonical keys at :783-784. The plan explicitly permits this and the source-facing SERIES_ONLY_FIELDS vocabulary justifies it, but a future reader may briefly wonder whether the bare names are a leftover.

tests/test_package.py now asserts non-null bound counts via Series.count(). That is the correct Polars semantics (count() excludes nulls), and it is what makes the 57,450/57,450 USGS expectation meaningful, but the intent would be clearer written as height - null_count().

Historical documents outside the write-set (docs/design/provider-redesign*.md, docs/milestones/**/plan.md, docs/provider_ports/*.md) still use bare start_date/end_date for the canonical carrier. This is correct under the plan's not-touched fence - they are records of prior states - and is noted only so a later reader does not mistake them for a missed rename.
summary:
PR #126 delivers the m1-s1 contract exactly. One commit (3c8ba5d) with the required subject, no attribution footer, no tag or version change, pr-body.md untracked and matching the mandated text; git diff --name-only over the range yields precisely the section-3 write-set (schema, thirteen generators, thirteen station_products.parquet, the named test carriers, ADR 0012 and 0014) and nothing else - no native.parquet, no tests/test_data, no CONTEXT.md, no ADR 0015, no pyproject.toml/uv.lock, no .pce file.

The binary rewrite is the part that could silently corrupt the package, so I verified it independently rather than trusting the pins: for all thirteen providers I read the base blob and the head blob straight out of git and ran polars.testing.assert_frame_equal(head.rename(inverse), base, check_exact=True). All thirteen pass. Row counts are 180/52145/16114/738/4155/33139/4092/194/44001/3903/1650/157548/8715, both bound columns are pl.Date at positions 6 and 7, and last_catalogue_check is unchanged per provider (2026-08-02, 2026-06-11, ..., 2025-10-10, ...) - i.e. nothing was regenerated and no value moved. All seven replaced content digests match the plan's authored values, and the USGS digest is correctly left alone because its helper hashes positional rows.

The rename is a pure key substitution in every generator: provider selection, availability, reasons, ordering, casts and validation are untouched, and the protected vocabulary survives - USGS SERIES_ONLY_FIELDS 'end_date', _matching_coverage source locals, the malformed-native test, ThaiWater query parameters, and requested_start_date/requested_end_date driver text. A word-boundary grep across src at the head ref shows the only bare-name hits are exactly those protected USGS source fields.

Test quality is genuinely strengthened, not merely renamed. test_internal_catalogue_schemas now asserts positively that 'start_date'/'end_date' are absent from the schema, and test_package.py's thirteen-provider loop gained exact row counts, the exact eight-column tuple, both Date dtypes, bare-name absence, and non-null bound counts (0 everywhere except USGS 57,450/57,450). Those would fail loudly on a partial rename, a regenerated artifact, or a dropped provider - which is precisely the regression class this change creates.

Gates re-run in the worktree at head: ruff format --check reports 162 files already formatted, ruff check passes with no suppressions added, ty check src passes, and the full suite is 1622 passed, 2 skipped (both skips are the pre-existing missing-folium skips) - identical to the stated baseline. git diff --check is silent and git status --short shows only ?? pr-body.md. The PR body's three claims each correspond to a real part of the diff. Nothing here should stop the merge.
